title: Daytime shelter procurement and 2024 financial results
subtitle: Also: revised code of conduct, community climate action report, committee terms of reference and year-end reserve transfers.
overview: The Committee of the Whole recommended that staff run a competitive procurement for daytime shelter services and report back through the 2026 budget update {{vote:m8}}. It also asks the Mayor to include funding and asks Wellington County to pay a share. Where a shelter should be located, especially in the downtown core, drew the most discussion.

The committee reviewed the 2024 year-end financial reports. It recommended covering a small tax-supported deficit and several service surpluses and deficits through reserve transfers, and advancing some 2026 capital budgets into 2025, including firefighter bunker gear and an affordable housing project. It received the long-term reserves and debt statement for information {{vote:m6}}.

It recommended approving a revised Code of Conduct for Council and Local Boards {{vote:m7}}, and approving updated committee terms of reference {{vote:m2}}. It also received the community climate action report and supported staff actions to carry it out {{vote:m9}}. All of these recommendations go to Council for final decision.
Earlier, a closed session on part of Grange Road ended with Council receiving information and giving direction to staff.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff run a competitive procurement for daytime shelter services and report back through the 2026 budget update, that the Mayor include funding, and that Wellington County be asked to pay 10 per cent.

The committee recommended allocating the 2024 tax-supported deficit and non-tax-supported surplus through transfers to and from named reserves, including library and police contingency reserves and the tax rate operating contingency reserve.

The committee recommended approving budget adjustments and advancing 2026 funding to 2025 for the parkland dedication by-law update, an affordable housing demonstration project and firefighter bunker gear, plus a transfer for building code file digitization.

The committee received the 2024 long-term financial statement for information and recommended reserve transfers, including a transfer to the Courts capital reserve fund and funding for the Elliott Community long-term care bed expansion.

decisions.item: Code of Conduct for Council and Local Boards
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the revised code, which applies to advisory committee members and sets rules on blocking people on social media and on using titles during campaigns.
The committee received the community climate action report and recommended approving staff actions to support collective climate action across the community.

decisions.item: Committee of the Whole terms of reference
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the revised Committee of the Whole terms of reference.

debate: On daytime shelter, several councillors supported the service but raised concerns, reported from downtown residents and the downtown business association, about locating it on the main downtown streets. They suggested a location near, but not on, those streets.

Another councillor noted that main streets include areas with existing social services, and asked staff to consider safety, security and past downtown investment costs. Staff said location limits could shrink the pool of bidders and that the request for proposals is not yet drafted.

On the code of conduct, one councillor worried that the social media blocking rules could discourage marginalized people from joining advisory committees and said amendments were being prepared. Staff said the rules apply where an account acts as a public forum on official duties, and the integrity commissioner can advise.

On the climate report, a delegate asked for staff time, meeting space, a convener role and shared information for community groups. Councillors questioned whether 2030 targets can be met and asked for stronger policy tools, such as district energy. Staff said the report sets practical actions and green development standards are being drafted.

On finances, councillors asked about falling reserves, development charge collections and rising workplace injury costs. Staff said reserves are expected to fall as large capital projects proceed and that a report on related employee policy is planned for June.
